result.title: GRAFT: Cross-Backbone LoRA Reuse for Continual Language and Multimodal Learning
result.summary: In continual learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning enables large language models to acquire new capabilities through lightweight adapters such as LoRA, yet the reuse of pretrained adapters is typically restricted to models sharing the same backbone. This limits the transfer of learned capabilities from language models to multimodal models. We propose GRAFT (Generalist Reuse of Adapters via Feature-space Transfer), a framework for cross-backbone LoRA reuse. GRAFT retrieves the most relevant pretrained LoRA adapter from a modality-aware library and maps it into the target backbone through a learned linear bridge between corresponding source and target feature spaces. We evaluate GRAFT on ten Super-NaturalInstructions text tasks, transferring Qwen2.5 LoRAs to Qwen2.5-VL, and five multimodal tasks, where Qwen2.5-VL LoRAs are directly reused. Compared with randomly initialized LoRA adapters, GRAFT improves performance on most evaluated tasks. These results show that GRAFT provides a simple and effective mechanism for reusing learned capabilities across language and multimodal models in continual learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GRAFT，从模态感知的 LoRA 适配器库中检索最相关的预训练适配器，并通过学习得到的源与目标特征空间之间的线性桥接，将其映射到不同 backbone 上复用；在十个文本指令任务（Qwen2.5→Qwen2.5-VL）和五个多模态任务上验证了该框架。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中的特征空间线性桥接可能为跨 backbone 的 latent 状态迁移与对齐提供可核查的轻量线索，但论文属于持续学习中的适配器复用，不涉及推理期视觉证据使用、动态计算或停止决策。
